title: Dangling AWS Route53 NS delegation on otc.wert.io enables hosted-zone-reclaim subdomain takeover (also affects demo.otc.wert.io)
vuln_class: Subdomain takeover / dangling DNS delegation (A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration)
repro: 1) curl -sS 'https://dns.google/resolve?name=wert.io&type=NS' (confirms Cloudflare parent NS). 2) curl -sS 'https://dns.google/resolve?name=otc.wert.io&type=NS' (returns Status 2 with EDE 22 at delegation + EDE 23 REFUSED from four Route53 IPs 205.251.197.90 / 205.251.195.78 / 205.251.193.212 / 205.251.198.85). 3) curl -sS -H 'accept: application/dns-json' 'https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=otc.wert.io&type=NS' (second-resolver cross-check). 4) curl -sS 'https://dns.google/resolve?name=demo.otc.wert.io&type=A' (inherits the same lame delegation). Proof-of-condition only, no AWS hosted zone was created.
impact: After reclaiming the Route53 hosted zone (create otc.wert.io in attacker-controlled AWS account until AWS assigns the four-NS set ns-846.awsdns-41.net / ns-1370.awsdns-43.org / ns-1621.awsdns-10.co.uk / ns-468.awsdns-58.com), the attacker is authoritative for otc.wert.io and every name under it. From there they can issue a browser-trusted DV TLS certificate via Let's Encrypt (DNS-01 or HTTP-01) and serve arbitrary HTTPS content under https://otc.wert.io/ and https://demo.otc.wert.io/. For a crypto/payments brand this enables pixel-perfect OTC-trading clones that capture wallet addresses, trade intents, API keys, KYC uploads and OTP codes, satisfies any *.wert.io origin/wildcard trust check performed by widget or partner iframes, and causes significant brand and regulatory exposure.
recommended_fix: In the Cloudflare zone for wert.io, delete every NS record on otc.wert.io and any explicit child delegation such as demo.otc.wert.io. If OTC functionality is still planned, create the Route53 hosted zone first, read the assigned NS set, then publish a fresh delegation. Enforce a tear-down checklist that always removes parent NS records before deleting a Route53 hosted zone. Audit the rest of the wert.io zone for additional dangling delegations or CNAMEs to decommissioned S3/CloudFront/Heroku/Vercel/Pages origins.

title: partner.wert.io /api/external/* three-state operation enumeration oracle
vuln_class: Information disclosure / observable response discrepancy (A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration)
repro: 1) curl -i -H 'X-Api-Key: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' https://partner.wert.io/api/external/orders -> HTTP 401 {"error":"ERR_UNAUTHORIZED","success":false} (path+verb exist, key wrong). 2) curl -i -X POST -H 'X-Api-Key: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' https://partner.wert.io/api/external/orders -> HTTP 400 {"error":"method not allowed"} (path exists, verb wrong). 3) curl -i -H 'X-Api-Key: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' https://partner.wert.io/api/external/webhooks -> HTTP 404 {"error":"no matching operation was found"} (path does not exist). 4) curl -i https://partner.wert.io/api/external/anything -> HTTP 400 {"msg":"Header parameter X-Api-Key is required, but not found"} (key missing).
impact: Unauthenticated enumeration of the complete external partner API operation matrix (verbs and paths) without any credential. Oracle also reproduces identically on partner-sandbox.wert.io and partner-green.wert.io. Alone, Medium information disclosure; combined with any future authentication or validation flaw on one of the enumerated operations, it is a direct enabler lowering the cost of credential-stuffing and 0-day-endpoint discovery.
recommended_fix: Normalise all pre-auth responses to a single opaque status (ideally HTTP 401 with a fixed body such as {"error":"ERR_UNAUTHORIZED"}) for unknown paths, unsupported verbs, missing keys and invalid keys. Alternatively, move the X-Api-Key validation in front of the go-openapi router so path/method matching does not occur until a valid key is presented, and keep detailed error strings behind the auth boundary.

title: Prometheus /metrics on cards-api.wert.io and cards-api-2.wert.io is publicly exposed, leaks internal pod IPs and service name
repro: 1) curl -sS https://cards-api.wert.io/metrics -> HTTP 200 text/plain, body includes cards_registrator_request_duration_seconds_bucket{host="10.20.129.110:8080",...} and go_info{version="go1.27.1"}. 2) curl -sS https://cards-api-2.wert.io/metrics -> HTTP 200, body includes host="10.20.129.223:8080". 3) curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://cards.wert.io/metrics -> 403 (fix baseline on sister host).
impact: Unauthenticated information disclosure: internal pod IPs (10.20.129.110:8080, 10.20.129.223:8080) and the pod CIDR 10.20.129.0/24, the backend plaintext port (8080), the service identity (cards_registrator), the Go runtime version (go1.27.1), process start-time and resource counters, and per-URL request/response histograms suitable for traffic-volume side channels. No credentials or PII in current payload, so it is a hardening gap rather than a direct breach, but it is a reconnaissance primitive that lowers the cost of any future SSRF, bastion or lateral-movement finding against the same cluster.
recommended_fix: Serve /metrics only to the Prometheus scraper: bind the metrics handler on an in-cluster-only port (e.g. --metrics-addr=:9090) or gate it with the same bearer token Prometheus supports, or an IP allow-list of the Prometheus pod's service IP. Mirror the ingress rule already applied on cards.wert.io (which correctly returns 403) onto cards-api.wert.io and cards-api-2.wert.io. Separately, drop the host label from the cards_registrator_* histograms so pod IPs never land in a counter.
